quests.question: The professor ___ lectures are always packed teaches on Tuesday mornings.
quests.hint: The lectures belong to the professor - which pronoun shows possession?
quests.explanation: 'Whose' shows that the lectures belong to the professor being described.

quests.question: All ___ the students needed was a little more time to prepare.
quests.hint: After 'all,' which pronoun is the standard, idiomatic choice?
quests.explanation: After 'all' used this way, 'that' is the standard relative pronoun.

quests.question: This is the easiest course ___ the school currently offers.
quests.hint: After a superlative like 'the easiest,' which pronoun is most natural?
quests.explanation: After superlatives, 'that' is the natural, idiomatic choice in everyday English.

quests.question: We discussed the students and the projects ___ impressed the judges most.
quests.hint: The clause covers both people AND things - which pronoun works for both?
quests.explanation: 'That' is used because the clause refers to a mix of people and things.

quests.question: The student ___ essay won the contest is only sixteen years old.
quests.hint: The essay belongs to the student - which pronoun shows that?
quests.explanation: 'Whose' connects the essay to the student it belongs to.

quests.question: This is the only classroom ___ has working air conditioning.
quests.hint: After 'the only,' which pronoun sounds most natural?
quests.explanation: After 'the only,' 'that' is the natural, idiomatic choice.

quests.question: Nothing ___ the teacher explained made sense to me at first.
quests.hint: After 'nothing,' which pronoun is the standard choice?
quests.explanation: 'That' is the standard relative pronoun after indefinite words like 'nothing.'

quests.question: The school ___ program was just ranked first hired three new teachers.
quests.hint: The program belongs to the school - which pronoun shows possession, even for a place?
quests.explanation: 'Whose' can show possession for institutions as well as people, so it fits here.

quests.question: This is the hardest exam ___ our class has ever taken.

quests.question: We packed the books and the notebooks ___ we needed for the exam.
quests.hint: Wait - both items here are things. Which pronoun still works, and reads naturally, for a simple list of things?
quests.explanation: 'That' works naturally for things in a defining clause, especially when listing several items together.

quests.question: This is the busiest week ___ our office has had all year.
